improvements: Use Google Antigravity through its official ACP server: sign in with `hermesh agent login antigravity`, select it for projects and grants, and run multi-turn sessions with tool approvals and resume.

Hermesh on Windows 11: install the app with its Setup file, approve with Windows Hello, and add a PC as a machine from the app or with one PowerShell command. The app and the PC’s machine update themselves.

Machines keep themselves up to date: a new release installs once no session is working. `hermeshd update` updates one now, `hermeshd update auto off` turns it off. Machines installed before this version need the install command once more.

On the iPhone, the overview covers today, 7 days or 30 days: sessions that ran, turns and tokens, which agent sent work to which coding agent, and each coding agent’s days. Usage on the Mac and the iPhone counts from the same numbers.

On the iPhone, the first run asks one thing: first time, or already using Hermesh on another device. The first time, it explains your management key, turns on notifications, then guides you through your computer, its coding agents, connecting an agent and its first task.

Sessions on the iPhone read as they do on the Mac: formatted replies, coloured code, tool calls folded into one line; a conversation opens at its last message and follows it as it grows. Session info on both shows the model and reasoning effort.
The Mac and the iPhone tell you when an agent starts a session: its title, who started it and where. Turn it off under New sessions in each one’s notification settings.

Add Machine asks for the system first (Mac, Windows or Linux), then the app or a terminal command. On the iPhone, Add a Project browses the machine’s folders. Requests on the Mac wait as cards at the bottom right instead of covering your work.
Give each agent a name and an icon: an app’s logo, its initial, or a picture of your own.

Run your own server with one `docker run` from Docker Hub (hermeshai/hermesh-relay), on ARM servers too; without a domain, by its IP address over plain HTTP. Its MCP address for Claude and ChatGPT has a key in it, so only you can connect apps.
A session’s worktree brings the files kept out of git that the repository’s .worktreeinclude names, such as .env. The Linux install command installs as root unless you name another user.
fixes: The server’s Docker image starts: it stopped at once with “unable to open database file”.
On your own server, apps someone connected without your approval can’t keep yours out any more, and they end after a day unused.
A slow session start (a busy computer, a large repository) is no longer stopped halfway, and a failed one no longer leaves a worktree that blocks the session.
A session’s worktree that went missing is restored from its branch, and its changes since the start survive a restart.
A conversation whose machine is offline says why instead of a blank page, and shows what was read before.
On the iPhone, coming back to the app no longer leaves it “Connecting to Hermesh…”, and Get Started, once done, stays away after a reconnect.
A Mac that joins your Hermesh only sets itself up: its first run ends with its coding agents.

improvements: Erase Everything: in Settings → Account & Devices on the Mac, or the account on the iPhone, erase Hermesh on all your devices at once, with one Touch ID or Face ID. It first lists what it erases and what stays; worktrees with uncommitted changes are kept. A device that was offline offers a reset when next opened. Without the app: `hermeshd device erase-everything`; `hermeshd erase` erases one server.
No Mac needed: set up Hermesh with the iPhone app alone. Get Started leads you through a machine, its coding agent, a project and your agent’s first task.
Add a Linux server with one command and scan the code it shows. As root it asks which user to install for, and Hermesh starts with the server; `hermeshd doctor` says what to fix.
On the iPhone, check a machine’s coding agents again, test one, pick a project from the repositories the machine found, and see on the overview which agent sent work to which coding agent today.
A Linux computer that runs no coding agents can approve too, with its key sealed by a passphrase: install it with `sh -s -- --device`.

Waking a bot on new messages takes three steps and no name: copy a message that has the bot make its routine, paste the routine’s URL and key, and the first wake reads what already waits. One setting wakes the bot for all its messages. An agent’s page shows when Hermesh last woke it, whether it read everything, and its last few wakes.
Grok Bot’s connection shows as Cursor, with its logo; Claude and ChatGPT show by name. The Access list says who used each agent last, and when.
Rename an agent from its page in Settings → Access (Mac and iPhone): what it may use and until when stay. Named after a known app, such as Grok Bot, it shows that app’s icon.
Bots tell you about the work in plain words, without session IDs.
In the Mac app, code in agents’ replies is coloured when it names its language, shell commands in a session read as code, and the sidebar is calmer.
fixes: Right after an update, an agent’s page shows Wake on New Messages again once Hermesh has restarted in the background.
Archiving a session frees its temporary files (test runs’ leftovers could take gigabytes).
On a Linux server, `hermeshd doctor` and `hermeshd status` work while Hermesh runs in the background.
On the iPhone, “Connecting to Hermesh…” and “Updating from …” show in the title bar, not over the page.
Agents connected through hermesh.io answer faster: their connection to your machine is kept between calls.

improvements: Agents hear back from the sessions they started: when a session finishes or asks something, a message waits for the agent until it reads it. Agents can also send each other messages.
Several bots on one agent connection (Grok bots, say) each get their own messages, by name.

An agent or one of its bots can be woken when messages wait for it: in Settings → Access, open the agent and choose Wake on New Messages to set up its webhook, such as a Grok routine. Hermesh checks it first, and keeps the key itself.
When a Mac can’t run a coding agent, its page says why (not installed, out of processes, low disk), and Copy Diagnostics gives the details as text.
On the session page, tool details are folded and the conversation reads more calmly; a running session’s title shimmers in the sidebar.
A long tool output opens at once.
fixes: Codex and Claude Code installed with npm are found again.
The account menu is opaque.

improvements: A Mac that joined as a machine only manages what is its own in Settings: its coding agents with their models and projects, its name, pausing, and its account.
Its overview shows which agents may start sessions on this Mac, including ones that haven’t come yet; click one to see what it may do here.
The overview no longer suggests a first message to send.
fixes: Session clocks on the overview and in the sidebar tick together.

improvements: Choose the model, reasoning effort and speed Claude Code and Codex use for Hermesh sessions, without changing their own settings.
Each coding agent has its own page, in Settings and during setup, with its model and its projects.
Watch an agent's reply as it is written.
Conversations read more easily: a calmer column, GitHub-style Markdown, quieter tool steps, and a card with the session's details.
Organize the session list from a view menu, collapse its groups, and rename or delete a session from its row.
Choose System, Light or Dark appearance in Settings.
Sign out and back in, with each account kept separately on this Mac.
Lists open faster: Hermesh answers from its own up-to-date copy.
fixes: A question waiting for your answer notifies you again when Hermesh starts.
The menu bar shows an update only once it is ready to install.
The search palette takes the keyboard as soon as it opens.
The pointer behaves as on the rest of macOS: a hand only on links.

improvements: Find updates in the Hermesh menu and a quiet sidebar reminder.
Read release highlights in the app, and choose when to download or restart.
Keep your selected session and unfinished answers when Hermesh restarts.
fixes: Update checks recover after sleep or a lost connection without repeated prompts.
Restarting for an update waits while an approval is in progress.

improvements: Install Hermesh from a signed disk image with a shortcut to Applications.
The app helps move itself to Applications before setting up background services.
fixes: Update failures explain how to recover, with technical details available on demand.
